messages:
From: Elaine Park <elaine@finops.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 29 Jun 2025 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Evidence and accountability for p50/p95 commitments

Hi Jordan,

Thanks again for the demo last week — team is excited about the latency profile on Redwood Hosted. Procurement needs to lock down the operational definition before we move to contract signatures. Two asks from our side: a clear definition of the p50/p95 measurement window and an evidence package we can review during vendor due diligence.

Specifically we need:
- Exact measurement window (rolling window? calendar day?).
- Aggregation method for p50/p95 (per-region or global, weighted by requests?).
- Any carveouts or grace rules (maintenance, regional failover, blackouts).
- Sample metric queries and an exportable CSV containing the last 30 days of p50/p95 calculations.

Attached is our standard "vendor SLO evidence" template — please populate and return. Also confirm whether Redwood will accept a 0.5% transient-outlier carveout for DDOS-induced spikes, and whether fallbacks to model-variants count as SLO failures.

We'd like to get this resolved by end of week so legal can finish the purchase order.

Best,
Elaine Park
Head of Procurement
FinOps.ai

From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
To: Elaine Park <elaine@finops.ai>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Jun 2025 09:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Evidence and accountability for p50/p95 commitments

Hi Elaine — thanks for the note and for sharing the template. Marcus (our infra lead) is cc'd with the technical details; I've also looped in Legal (Kimberly) on a follow-up for contract language later today. Below is our proposed approach so you have something concrete to review immediately.

Summary (short):
- Measurement window: rolling 24h windows evaluated every minute, but contractual reporting will be on UTC calendar-day aggregates for billing / SLA reconciliation (we can map both).
- Aggregation: per-region p50/p95 computed on request latencies, plus a global weighted p95 for cross-region reporting.
- Carveouts: scheduled maintenance windows and provider-side network blackouts are carveouts; we propose a transient-outlier rule limited to 0.1% rather than 0.5% for DDOS-like events, subject to forensic evidence.
- Model fallback: automatic fallback to a compatible model variant that preserves output correctness will not be counted as an SLO failure; manual operator fallback will be considered a failure.

What we'll deliver this week:
1) Populated slo-evidence-template.xlsx with sample p50/p95 CSV for the last 30 days (per-region and global columns).
2) redwood-p50p95-sample-queries.txt with PromQL + example SQLs used to compute the quantiles.
3) A short technical note on measurement epoch, sampling, and outlier handling (Marcus will attach).

Open items we need from you:
- Confirmation that procurement is okay with rolling-24h evaluation and UTC calendar-day contractual reporting.
- Whether FinOps requires the 30-day CSV to be delivered to their procurement portal or uploaded to a signed secure folder (we can do either).

Timing: we'll target delivery of the initial evidence package by EOD today and a brief sync tomorrow morning if you want to walk through the queries.

Thanks,
Jordan Blake
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
Phone: +1 415-555-0142

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Jun 2025 11:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Evidence and accountability for p50/p95 commitments (technical note)

Jordan / Kimberly — attaching the short technical note here (pasted below). I'll also upload the query file and a sample CSV to the secure drive referenced by Jordan.

--- technical note (summary) ---
Measurement epoch and frequency:
- We compute latency per request at the point of response completion (server-side).
- Per-region quantiles are computed on raw request latencies using TDigest aggregation with 1-minute buckets; we roll these into a rolling 24-hour window (sliding) and also materialize calendar-day aggregates at 00:00 UTC.
Sampling and cardinality:
- For extremely high-volume routes (>10k rps sustained), we use deterministic sampling (1:10k) with reservoir correction to estimate the true quantiles; sample-aware error bounds are provided in the exported CSV.
Outlier handling and carveouts:
- Scheduled maintenance windows declared >2 business days in advance are excluded.
- We will apply a transient-outlier carveout only with forensic evidence of provider-agnostic network saturation or malicious traffic; proposed policy: up to 0.1% of requests per-day may be excluded, with a maximum single-event carveout of 30 minutes unless mutually agreed.
- Model-variant fallbacks: automatic variant switch that preserves the API response contract (same tokens/schema) is treated as a non-failure; human-initiated rollbacks count as failures.
Delivery artifacts:
- sample CSV columns: timestamp_utc, region, route, total_requests, p50_ms, p95_ms, sample_rate, excluded_requests, notes
- sample queries included (PromQL and SQL) and a short script to materialize tdigests.
Retention and audit:
- Raw request logs retained for 90 days; aggregated tdigests retained for 365 days.

If Kimberly has legal commentary on the carveout thresholds we should fold that into the contract language.

Marcus Lin
Sr. Infra Engineer | Redwood Inference

3) Carveouts: scheduled maintenance excluded; transient-outlier carveout capped at 0.1% per day and requires forensic evidence.
